summary: The candidate is correct and complete. The slab estimate gives uniform Lipschitz control, including as continuous normal components become small; vertical normals do not lower the infimum because each is approximated by nonvertical caps whose limiting mass is no greater. The truncated depth functions are jointly continuous minima, decrease uniformly to the continuous depth, and have interior maximizers. Separation of an unbalanced active set yields a uniform strict gain inside the anchor fiber, proving exact continuous-normal balance. A convergent subsequence fixes one interior maximizer, and moving the finitely many active caps to it costs only the stated Lipschitz error while preserving balance exactly. The weighted-sum contradiction proves the union cover, and the weighted centerpoint bound, subadditivity, and Caratheodory bound give the constants in the conclusion. The cylinder calculation, balanced normalized normals, vertical limit, and failed primitive-slice threshold are all exact, including at N=1.
